mechanism_narrative: A low federal funds rate indicates easy monetary conditions, which may stimulate borrowing and investment, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 days.
failure_condition: If FEDFUNDS is low but SPX returns are negative more than 50% of the time, this hypothesis is falsified.

mechanism_narrative: A rising unemployment rate suggests economic weakness, which may lead to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 days.
failure_condition: If UNRATE rises above 8% but SPX returns are positive more than 40% of the time, this hypothesis is falsified.

mechanism_narrative: When employment (PAYEMS) grows while unemployment (UNRATE) is high, it indicates labor market contradictions, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 days.
failure_condition: If both PAYEMS growth and high UNRATE occur but SPX returns are positive more than 50% of the time, this hypothesis is falsified.

mechanism_narrative: High retail sales (RSAFS) during an economic expansion indicate strong consumer demand, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 days.
failure_condition: If RSAFS is high during expansion but SPX returns are negative more than 40% of the time, this hypothesis is falsified.

mechanism_narrative: Rising industrial production (INDPRO) signals increased economic activity, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 days.
failure_condition: If INDPRO rises but SPX returns are negative more than 50% of the time, this hypothesis is falsified.

mechanism_narrative: A decline in housing starts (HOUST) below 800 thousand units suggests reduced demand, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 days.
failure_condition: If HOUST falls below 800 but SPX returns are positive more than 50% of the time, this hypothesis is falsified.

mechanism_narrative: When GDP growth (GDPC1) is strong but inflation (CPIAUCSL) is high, it may lead to monetary tightening, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 days.
failure_condition: If GDPC1 growth and CPIAUCSL increase occur but SPX returns are positive more than 50% of the time, this hypothesis is falsified.

mechanism_narrative: A rising federal funds rate during a tightening cycle may increase borrowing costs, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 days.
failure_condition: If FEDFUNDS rises above 4% during tightening but SPX returns are positive more than 40% of the time, this hypothesis is falsified.
